title: Magnetic Properties of High-Entropy Alloy FeCoNiTi

recollection.starting_material: guess – elemental powders of Fe, Co, Ni and Ti mixed in equiatomic or near-equiatomic proportions
recollection.intervention: guess – mechanical alloying followed by spark-plasma or arc melting and homogenizing heat treatment
recollection.structure: guess – single-phase face-centered-cubic (FCC) solid solution with minor Ti-rich precipitates
recollection.mechanism: guess – Ti addition distorts the lattice and enhances ferromagnetic exchange by modifying electronic density of states while precipitates pin domain walls
recollection.results: guess – saturation magnetization ~1.2–1.4 T, coercivity 200–400 A/m, Curie temperature above 900 K

score.note: The synthesis route is largely incorrect despite mentioning arc melting as one guess; it misses rapid quenching and the C14-dominant comparison alloy. The proposed single-phase FCC structure contradicts the observed FCC+C14 dual phase. Domain-wall pinning and density-of-states effects are generically relevant, but the key antiferromagnetic sublattice coupling, orbital contribution, spin canting, and phase-specific transitions are missing. The coercivity is far from 667 Oe, and the transition temperatures and saturation magnetization are not correctly recalled.
